subject: info-f-d
title: INFO.F.D.------ALT.F.
description: Diagram in WAC-35. INFO-F-D (information focus distortion) is crossed with ALT-F (alternative functionalism): a structurally pointed pairing — the question is what distortion-of-information-focus does to alternative functionalism. Information focus distortion is one of Braxton's diagnostic terms for what western interpretive practice has done to alternative work (Partch, Ives, Cowell, etc.), and the diagram poses what alternative functionalism becomes once that distortion is operative. ALT-F → SOC-RT (social reality), with SOC-RT also feeding the subject INFO-F-D and PRI-INFO (primary information). (C)STF (the *concept* of source transfer) → SPT-AW (spiritual awareness), and a *dashed* edge SPTC-D (spectacle diversion) → STF registers that the link from spectacle-diversion to source-transfer is conditional — a mediated relation, marking how spectacle can become source-transfer only under specific conditions. INFO-F-D also outputs to SPT-AW and to IST-S-ALGN (isolated systematic alignment, *dashed*). SPT-AW → INDIV-DY-RT (individual dynamic reality). Structural argument: information focus distortion crossed with alternative functionalism does not collapse the alternative — it routes through social reality (which feeds back into information-focus-distortion itself, a feedback loop) into primary information *and* through spiritual awareness into individual dynamic reality. The dashed edges to spectacle-diversion-as-source-transfer and to isolated-systematic-alignment encode Braxton's structural critique: the distorted alternative tends to register as spectacle-source-transfer only conditionally, and the systematic-alignment loss is also a conditional outcome — meaning the WAC section closes by making the precarity of alternative functionalism diagrammatically visible.
